Fun Facts

  • This station is the first Checkpoint ever built in Los Sengas Division and Nazca Railway as a whole.The Checkpoint Station Class did not exist in Terracept Division.</ref>
  • This station already had all the station facilities upon construction. Therefore, when Upgrading Works took place at this station, only the Departure Routines of the 8 platforms had to be updated.
  • At the time of this station's construction, checkpoint refers to stations which serve as the transport hub at the edge of its respective district, and therefore featured new station facilities, such as Los Sengas Coffee, advertisement boards and Station Art. However, not all the new facilities would be adopted in later stations and Upgrading Works of the Season 1 Stations.
  • The station art at the center of the station depicts the four seasons, namely Spring (Northeast), Summer (Southeast), Fall (Southwest) and Winter (Northwest). While , , and gateways would go on to be situated at the southeast, southwest, northwest and northeast respectively, this may have been the inspiration for the setting up of Group 2 Gateways. Coincidentially, the Station Icon of this Station also incorporates elements of the station icons from the four Group 2 Gateways.
  • The design of this station pays tribute to Terracept Terminal.
  • This station is the permanent Down Direction terminus of , with a set of Turn Back Sidings to the east of this station.
  • The Platforms of this station have been sealed off for four years and eleven months before was established.This station began services on August 8 2015, but Centopia did not begin services until July 31 2020.</ref>
  • This station is the first station to feature two Station Control Rooms, and was the only station with such a layout at the time of its construction.

History

Originally, Sanfo Island had mountainous terrain. In order to facilitate urban development, all the mountains on this island were razed down, and the shoreline has also undergone reclamation in order to straighten the coast.
